title: ARC four-season yurt house cost model

owner_builder.label: Owner-builder
owner_builder.description: Owner labour reduces cash expenditure and remains visible as imputed value.

mixed_labour.label: Mixed labour
mixed_labour.description: A planning split between paid trades and owner work; adjust when a work plan or quotation exists.

contractor_built.label: Contractor-built
contractor_built.description: All owner-eligible construction labour is treated as paid labour at the selected planning rate.

arc_household_systems.label: ARC household systems
arc_household_systems.description: The existing ARC low-cost package: roof rainwater collection, first flush, indoor food-grade storage, demand pump, sediment filtration, UV, under-sink RO, compact PEX, private shower, drainless composting toilet, approved greywater pathway, off-grid electricity and seasonal hot water.

generic_well_septic_grid.label: Generic well / septic / grid alternatives
generic_well_septic_grid.description: Site-specific alternative placeholders retained for sites where the ARC household package cannot be approved.

centralized_shared_services.label: Centralized shared services
centralized_shared_services.description: Household water, sanitation and electrical capital is removed from the dwelling layer and must be quoted in the shared-infrastructure layer. No centralized quote is invented here.

tax_rate.note: Ontario HST treatment, rebates and owner-builder eligibility require project-specific CRA review.

water_plumbing_sanitation.source_note: Historical ARC package detail supplied with the original design brief; the package total, included qualified plumbing labour and permit allowance are treated as one inclusive package.

hot_water.source_note: Historical ARC package detail supplied with the original design brief; the CAD 400 integration allowance is inside the CAD 2,000 package.

household_electrical.source_note: Historical ARC package detail supplied with the original design brief; the CAD 700 qualified electrical labour and CAD 100 inspection allowance are inside the CAD 3,300 package.

components.label: Platform / foundation
components.source_note: Foundation geometry and site loads require design; Ontario tiny-home guidance confirms footing/foundation and anchorage review. Structural base and floor framing exclude finish flooring.

components.label: Yurt frame and tension structure
components.source_note: Canadian yurt supplier specifications support diameter, lattice, rafters, crown/dome and cable as distinct physical elements; this row is limited to the wall/tension system and structural sizing remains engineered.

components.label: Roof structure and covering
components.source_note: Actual sloping roof area is calculated from radius and roof pitch; this row covers the pitched roof structure and covering, not wall air/water control.

components.label: Insulation
components.source_note: Ontario guidance requires year-round energy efficiency and insulation; exact assembly requires envelope design.

components.label: Weatherproofing and air control
components.source_note: Water, moisture and draft control are required design outcomes; this row covers wall air/water control, flashing and sealing and excludes the roof covering.

components.label: Windows / dome glazing
components.source_note: Canadian suppliers publish standard window/dome options and limits; thermal performance and framing are design-specific.

components.label: Exterior and interior doors
components.source_note: Canadian yurt supplier standard door and jamb packages provide a market-spec reference; installed code-compliant openings require confirmation.

components.label: Basic privacy partition
components.dimensions: 3.0 m partition length × 2.4 m height = 7.2 m² gross panel area
components.material_spec: 38 × 89 mm SPF framing, 12.7 mm plywood panels, trim, fasteners, sealant and washable protective coating
components.source_note: Minimal privacy enclosure takeoff; 7.2 m² of panel area and 1.5 person-hours/m² for cutting, fastening and sealing. Material price is an explicit planning synthesis; final fire, moisture and accessibility details require design.

components.label: Protective floor surface
components.dimensions: Selected usable floor area, 63.0425 m² at the 9.144 m reference diameter
components.material_spec: Two-coat water-based floor sealer/paint over the supplier-excluded platform deck; no decorative flooring or new structural deck
components.source_note: Minimal protective treatment for the existing platform deck, priced per actual usable floor area. Product coverage, moisture compatibility and final finish require a local product selection and quote.

components.label: Interior decorative surface finish
components.dimensions: Selected usable floor area as a transparent proxy for a small interior finish scope; final wall-area takeoff required
components.material_spec: Low-VOC interior coating and trim allowance only; no cabinetry or utility fixtures
components.source_note: Elective surface treatment. It is excluded from the minimal completed preset until a wall-area takeoff and finish selection are made.

components.label: Upper-floor structure and load path
components.source_note: Two-storey/loft structure requires span, support, connection and foundation engineering; diameter alone cannot establish feasibility.

components.label: Stairs and access opening
components.source_note: Stairs, guards and opening are included as separate upper-floor consequences; code review required.

components.label: Loft guards / edge protection
components.source_note: Guard geometry is layout-specific and requires building-code confirmation.

components.label: Basic kitchen counter
components.dimensions: 1.8 m counter length × 0.6 m depth = 1.08 m²
components.material_spec: 18 mm laminated or sealed plywood work surface with edge trim and wall protection
components.source_note: Minimal food-preparation surface only. No cabinets, appliances, sink or faucet are included here; sink and shower fixtures remain in the utility package.

components.label: Kitchen base cabinetry
components.dimensions: One approximately 1.8 m base-cabinet run; final cabinet layout required
components.material_spec: Basic modular or site-built base cabinets with doors and shelves
components.source_note: Elective storage upgrade; excluded from the minimal completed preset until a cabinet layout and product quote are selected.

components.label: Basic kitchen appliances
components.dimensions: One compact appliance set; exact loads and appliances require selection
components.material_spec: Optional compact cooking/refrigeration appliances; no utility service upgrade included
components.source_note: Elective appliance package. Excluded by default because the utility package does not establish appliance selection or electrical demand.

components.label: Optional bathroom storage and trim
components.dimensions: One compact storage/trim set; final wet-area layout required
components.material_spec: Open shelving, towel hardware and protective trim only
components.source_note: Optional non-plumbing fit-out. The existing utility package already contains the sink, private shower, composting toilet, plumbing installation and commissioning.

components.label: Heating appliance and system
components.source_note: Existing ARC winter masonry-heater concept; appliance, chimney/fire safety and installation require design confirmation.

components.label: Ventilation / air exchange
components.source_note: Ontario guidance recommends HVAC appropriate to small year-round spaces; system selection requires design.

components.label: Household electrical equipment
components.source_note: Existing ARC approximately 400 Wh/day, 400 W PV, MPPT, 2.52 kWh nominal flooded lead-acid storage and 1,000 W pure-sine inverter; inclusive package labour and inspection allowance are decomposed in the service-package record.

components.label: Water, plumbing and sanitation package
components.source_note: Inclusive ARC package: fixtures, toilet, excavation, compact plumbing, commissioning, included qualified plumbing labour and permit allowance are counted once in the package total.

components.label: Domestic hot water package
components.source_note: Inclusive ARC winter thermosiphon and summer solar-thermal package; integration labour is included once in the package total.

components.label: Household demand upgrade
components.source_note: Explicit allowance for larger household storage, fixtures and electrical demand; replace with a design takeoff.

components.label: Delivery and logistics
components.source_note: Distance, access, crane/hauling and seasonal road conditions require a quotation.

components.label: Equipment hire
components.source_note: Lifting, access and foundation equipment vary with site and layout.

components.label: Design and engineering
components.source_note: Yurt structural system, snow/wind loads, fire separation, envelope, foundation and servicing require qualified design.

components.label: Permits and approvals
components.source_note: Ontario requires building permits for tiny homes; local permit/development fees depend on the approving municipality and project.

threshold_rules.label: Diameter above 9.144 m
threshold_rules.source: Structural system must be engineered for span, snow and wind loads; the model exposes a planning threshold rather than an approval rule.

threshold_rules.label: Diameter above 10.668 m
threshold_rules.source: Larger span and load-path review required; supplier and engineer quotation needed.

threshold_rules.label: Roof pitch above 35 degrees
threshold_rules.source: Planning allowance for changed roof geometry and connections; not a code threshold.

threshold_rules.label: Loft or second storey
threshold_rules.source: Upper floor creates additional structure, access, guards and load-path design; design approval required.

legacy_scope_components.scope: Reinforced insulated structure, platform, masonry heater and chimney
Fixtures, toilet, excavation, compact plumbing, commissioning, CAD 1,200 qualified plumbing labour and CAD 600 permit allowance
Winter thermosiphon and summer solar-thermal hot water, including CAD 400 integration labour
Approximately 400 W PV, MPPT, 2.52 kWh nominal battery, 1,000 W inverter, CAD 700 qualified electrical labour and CAD 100 inspection allowance

legacy_arc_benchmark.note: The historical exact sum is CAD 61,240 (CAD 50,000 + CAD 5,940 + CAD 2,000 + CAD 3,300); the public CAD 61,000 figure was rounded. The original itemized structural quote was not recovered. The audited model preserves this reference beside its independently itemized scope.

yurts_canada_purchased_package.label: Yurts Canada purchased-package route
yurts_canada_purchased_package.scope_note: The 30 ft Base Kit is a supplier package with published inclusions and exclusions. Platform, household systems, heating, delivery, design, tax and contingency are separate model layers.

local_fabrication_owner_built.label: Local fabrication or owner-built route
local_fabrication_owner_built.basis: No independently supported bill of materials is currently available in the evidence set.
local_fabrication_owner_built.note: The historical ARC approximately CAD 61,000 benchmark is not a local-fabrication price and must not be inferred as one. A local route requires its own documented materials, labour, design and approval basis.

former_model_reference.basis: Default 9.144 m single-storey ARC household systems, central rates, mixed labour, 13% tax, 8% contingency; generated immediately before package-boundary correction.

accounting_rules: A component is assigned one physical driver and appears once in the completed dwelling total.

The ARC household utility package is carried forward once as water/plumbing/sanitation 5,940 CAD, hot water 2,000 CAD and electrical 3,300 CAD. Included paid labour and fees are decomposed for audit but are not added again. Sink, shower, toilet and their installation remain inside that package; bathroom fittings outside those fixtures are optional.
Centralized servicing removes the corresponding household component from resident dwelling capital and exposes the unresolved cost as a shared-infrastructure quotation requirement.
Owner labour reduces upfront cash but remains visible as owner hours and imputed value; professional work is not treated as owner-replaceable.
Taxes and contingency are explicit additions. They are not used to force agreement with the legacy CAD 61,000 benchmark.
A custom completed-dwelling quote overrides financing headline value but leaves the modelled component ledger and unallocated quote difference visible.
